solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Check on cereal in local store

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on (after) another follows it

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain, eaten as a breakfast cereal
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone checks the breakfast cereal on the shelves of the shop round the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is one outlet of a chain, the shop in your neighbourhood rather than the head office.

clue.text: Deprived female wearing cap

indicators.note: the cap is worn around the female, so it encloses her letter

parts.note: a beret is a soft flat cap

explanation.surface: A woman stripped of everything but the cap on her head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means having lost or been robbed of something, a close synonym of deprived.

clue.text: A new banknote's to be announced, one feels

indicators.note: announcing something means saying it out loud, so the letters are judged by their sound

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; N is a standard abbreviation for new; a tenner is a ten-pound banknote; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A fresh banknote is about to be unveiled to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: A-N-TENNER said aloud sounds like the answer. A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's antenna is its feeler, the organ it uses to touch and sense things.

clue.text: Short piece of film has Conservative on edge

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece sitting on another is written above it

parts.note: a lip is the rim or edge of a cup or crater

explanation.surface: A news snippet shows a Tory looking nervous and on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a brief extract from a film or broadcast.

clue.text: Ruler gives extremely tacky and intemperate speech

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two outermost letters

parts.note: a rant is a wild, angry tirade

explanation.surface: A tasteless, raging speech is what a despot delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel, absolute ruler, a despot.

clue.text: US park is which some yeti is roaming

indicators.note: letters that roam wander off into a new order

explanation.surface: A Himalayan snowman has wandered into an American national park.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a famous national park in California.

clue.text: In a compound, small tree

indicators.note: the small letter sits in the words that follow it

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure or compound for animals

explanation.surface: A little tree is growing inside a walled compound.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a kind of poplar with trembling leaves.

clue.text: Getting up to dry fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: Rising to hang a catch of fish out to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large flatfish prized for eating.

clue.text: Wine is nastier when drunk

indicators.note: drunk means mixed up and reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that this wine tastes worse once you have downed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Everything finishes convincingly

parts.note: all means everything
ends up means finishes or winds up

explanation.surface: A satisfied declaration that everything comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything finishes' reads as the definition; in fact it is the wordplay, and 'convincingly' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone all ends up is an idiom for winning thoroughly and decisively.

clue.text: Really excellent police officer

definitions.meaning: short for superintendent, a senior police rank

explanation.surface: Praise for an outstanding policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Super works both as an enthusiastic adjective for first-rate and as informal shorthand for a superintendent.

clue.text: Come across heartless devil

indicators.note: without its heart, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: a fiend is a devil or demon

explanation.surface: Encountering a cruel, pitiless demon.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to come upon or discover it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: I'm pink, burning with love

definitions.note: the answer speaks of itself: a noun for the bird, which could say this

parts.note: flaming means burning
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone blushing bright pink with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a wading bird famous for its pink feathers, so it might describe itself this way.

clue.text: I'm on the phone still

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece sitting on another is written above it

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe
a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they are busy on a call.
explanation.definitionFit: Immobile means motionless, not moving at all.

clue.text: Carpet a church, around cross

indicators.note: the words before it go around the cross

parts.note: a minster is a large or important church
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Laying a carpet in a church, around the cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven carpet named after the Devon town where it was first made.

clue.text: Was in charge of big bag for plunder

parts.note: ran means managed or was in charge of
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: A boss who ran a large bag for collecting loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search a place thoroughly and rob it.

clue.text: Inspector left a dainty piece of food

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of novels and television

explanation.surface: A detective leaves behind a delicate titbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a famous British TV detective, from Colin Dexter's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small, tasty mouthful of food.

clue.text: Silly person crosses one line in the half-dark

indicators.note: the fool straddles the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a twit is a fool
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fool stumbles across a line in the dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit describes something lit only by twilight, the dim half-light of dusk.

clue.text: No heroes worked in such a small town

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; a one-horse town is just such a small town

indicators.note: worked means reshaped or kneaded, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: In a sleepy little town, nobody heroic ever had a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is an idiom for a tiny, dull, insignificant place.

clue.text: First of teeth, perfect, coming up, do this?

definitions.text: First of teeth, perfect, coming up, do this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: pure means flawless or perfect

explanation.surface: A baby's first perfect tooth breaking through the gum.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: when a first tooth comes up through the gum, it is said to erupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists say a tooth erupts when it breaks through the gum.

clue.text: Be aware of hearing refusal

indicators.note: in a hearing, the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Realising that one's request has been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something is to be conscious or informed of it.

clue.text: One maintaining uprightness in wild orgy

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A moralist keeping upright standards amid a debauched party.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyro, short for gyroscope, is a spinning device used to keep craft stable and level.

clue.text: Arab in USA I'd relocated

indicators.note: relocated means moved elsewhere, so the letters change place

explanation.surface: An Arab saying they have moved to America.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saudi is a native of Saudi Arabia, an Arab country.

clue.text: Barrier at site entrance: parking, indeed with everyone

parts.note: ay is an old word for yes, indeed
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A gate at a building site where everyone must park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'site' is a website, not a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: A paywall blocks web content until the reader pays, a barrier at the door of a website.

clue.text: What a setter, or anyone antisocial, may drop

definitions.text: What a setter, or anyone antisocial, may drop

parts.words: What a setter, or anyone antisocial, may drop
parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, which drops (gives birth to) young; a lout drops rubbish in the street

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler, or any lout, might let something fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is both a brood of puppies born together and rubbish dropped carelessly.

clue.text: Spaceship alien lands on Gibraltar?

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece landing on another comes after it

parts.note: the Rock is the nickname of Gibraltar; the question mark flags an example
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A UFO touches down on the Rock of Gibraltar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is a vehicle propelled into space, a spacecraft.
